rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Writing on Morgan's behalf (I help manage the Halcyon Threshold inbox). Thanks for thinking of the project. Morgan isn't able to go on the record this week due to a pending employment-disclosure matter, so we'll have to pass on a named quote before your Tuesday deadline. Good luck with the story, Halcyon Threshold (for Morgan Hale) morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Tessa Brandt (Larkin Dispatch):** politely declined the named quote before her Tuesday deadline, door left open

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Writing on Morgan Hale's behalf. Thank you for the invitation to sign the open letter. Morgan won't be signing at this time — please do not list his name or Halcyon Threshold as signatories. He has a policy of not putting his name to public statements until a pending employment-disclosure matter is resolved, and of personally reviewing any policy position before endorsing it. He may be in a position to engage with future efforts, so please do keep Halcyon Threshold on your list for future correspondence. Best regards, Halcyon Threshold (for Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Corvid Institute:** declined the open-letter sign-on for now; asked that your name/org not be listed.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Writing on Morgan's behalf (I help with the Halcyon Threshold inbox) — thank you, this is a genuinely useful offer, and five hours a week of data-analyst time is exactly the shape of help the project needs. The concrete thing we're scoping right now: a structured index of publicly published frontier-AI evaluations — what safety-relevant things are being measured, by whom, how often, and what's not being measured at all. The first task would be bounded: collecting and verifying an initial set of entries (source, risk area, methodology, date) in a shared sheet. Very much a data-collection-and-verification job before it becomes anything fancier. Morgan will follow up personally this week to say hello properly and agree on scope. Does that kind of first task sound like a fit for your hours? Thanks again, Halcyon Threshold (for Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Priya Raman:** warmly accepted her offer, proposed the eval-index data collection as her first bounded task, and committed you to a personal follow-up this week.
